{"path":"/study","markdown":"# Verification report: square-duct

foam-verify 0.0.1, from `study.toml`: 2 levels, finest first; refined = mesh; grid sequence structured; refined directions d = 2; formal order 2.

## Verdict

**Not a clean pass.** 0 of 1 quantity of interest are clean passes.

| QoI | Finest grid | Relative U | Grid convergence | Clean pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fRe` | 56.8997 +/- 0.0257 | 0.045% | two grids, p assumed | no |

What stops a clean pass:

- `fRe`: two-grid estimate at an assumed order of accuracy
- `fRe`: only two grids: the observed order cannot be estimated, so the GCI assumes the formal order p = 2 with Fs = 3 (Roache); a third grid is needed to check it

## Levels

| Level | Folder | Cells | r to the next coarser |
|---|---|---|---|
| 160x160 | `n160` | 25,600 | 2.000 |
| 80x80 | `n80` | 6,400 |  |

- dim = 2 with no empty or wedge patches: patches inlet and outlet have one face per cell on every level, so the mesh is one cell across them and that direction is not refined

## Settings consistency

**Pass.** The levels differ only in the mesh.

Compared on every level: `system/fvSchemes`, `system/fvSolution`, `system/fvOptions`, `constant/transportProperties`, `constant/turbulenceProperties`, `0/U`, `0/p`, `system/controlDict`.

## `fRe`

**Not a clean pass.** 56.8997 +/- 0.0257 (GCI at an assumed order, 0.045%); band 56.8740 to 56.9254.

From `postProcessing/wallStress/*/surfaceFieldValue.dat`, column `areaAverage(wallShearStress)`, x component, last value, times -800; window: the last 10% of the samples, at least 50.

| Check | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Grid convergence | fail | grids 1-2: two-grid estimate at an assumed order of accuracy |
| Refinement ratio | pass | r21 = 2.000; at least 1.3 (Celik et al. 2008, step 2) |
| Observed order | assumed | two grids: p is taken as the formal order, 2, with Fs = 3 (Roache) |
| Asymptotic range | n/a | checked only for monotonic convergence |
| Coarser triplets | n/a | 2 grids: no coarser triplet |
| Iterative convergence | pass | converged on every level (tol 0.001) |
| Iterative error | pass | largest u_it / U = 1.6e-09 (160x160), within 1/100 (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4) |
| Settings consistency | pass | the levels differ only in the mesh (8 files compared) |
| Refined directions | pass | dim = 2 with no empty or wedge patches: patches inlet and outlet have one face per cell on every level, so the mesh is one cell across them and that direction is not refined |
| Refinement scope | assumed | scope mesh: assumes every cell, near-wall layers included, was refined by the same ratio (Celik et al. 2008, step 2: systematic refinement, geometrically similar cells) |
| Grid sequence | assumed | grid sequence structured: the levels refine one base grid systematically (the base grid may itself be unstructured), so Fs = 1.25 with three or more grids (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4.1) |

| Level | Value | Iterative | Window | Relative range | Relative drift | u_it | u_it / U |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 160x160 | 56.89972 | converged | 80 of 800, 7210 to 8000 | 1.4e-12 | -1.4e-12 | 4.0e-11 | 1.6e-09 |
| 80x80 | 56.87400 | converged | 80 of 800, 7210 to 8000 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Richardson extrapolation, grids 1-2: phi_ext = 56.90830, e_a = 0.045%, e_ext = 0.015%, GCI_fine = 0.045%, Fs = 3.

## Method

- Grid convergence after Celik et al. (2008), with the convergence types of Eça and Hoekstra (2014): Fs = 1.25 on three or more grids of a structured grid sequence, and 3 for an unstructured sequence (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4.1), on two grids, or when p is outside [0.5, 4]; refinement ratios of at least 1.3; an asymptotic-range ratio within [0.9, 1.1]; with four or more grids, every coarser triplet converges monotonically too. Above the formal order, U uses the formal order (ASME V&V 20, Appendix C-4); the Richardson numbers and the checks keep the observed p. An oscillatory triplet gets a spread bound and never a clean pass (foam-verify docs/gci.md).
- Iterative convergence of each QoI from its own history over the window given with it: converged when its relative range and relative drift are within tol, and u_it is half the range. On the grids behind the result, u_it must be at most U/100 (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4; docs/iterative.md).
- Settings consistency: the schemes, solver settings, physical properties, boundary conditions and near-wall layer settings of the levels, compared entry by entry (docs/consistency.md).
- U is the uncertainty of the finest-grid value, and the band is that value +/- U. A QoI is a clean pass only when no check fails (docs/report.md).
"}

content.text:
No. With only two grid levels, the study can't show that fRe is mesh-independent.

**What the study has**
- **Grids:** two levels, 80×80 (6,400 cells) and 160×160 (25,600 cells), with a refinement ratio of 2.
- **Values:** fRe is 56.87400 on the coarse grid and 56.89972 on the fine grid.
- **Iterative convergence:** passes. On the fine grid, fRe varies by about 1e-12 (relative) over the last 80 of 800 samples, so iterative error is negligible.
- **Settings:** pass. The schemes, solver settings, properties, boundary conditions and controlDict are the same on both levels, so only the mesh differs.

**Why it can't be called converged**
You need at least three grids to measure the observed order of accuracy p. With two, the GCI has to assume p equals the formal order of 2 and uses a safety factor of 3. That gives:

- Richardson extrapolation: 56.9083
- GCI on the fine grid: 0.045%, so U ≈ 0.026
- Band: 56.874 to 56.925

That U only holds if the solution really is converging at second order, and two grids can't test that. The verification report lists this as the only thing stopping a clean pass. There is no reference value in study.toml.

**What would settle it:** run a third level, such as 40×40 or 320×320, with the same settings. That would measure p, check whether the grids are in the asymptotic range, and give a GCI you can defend.

Until then, the best estimate is fRe = 56.900 ± 0.026, which is a 95% uncertainty at the assumed order. It is not a verified mesh-independent result.

FINAL: converged=no; value=56.8997; uncertainty=0.0257
